items.titleEn: EU probes Booking.com over online fraud risks
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: The European Union opened an investigation into online travel agent Booking.com on Wednesday over alleged failures to tackle fake listings and phishing scams. The EU fears Booking.com has underestimated the impact of fraud and unlicensed accommodation, and is not sufficiently protecting users' data from being misused for scams.

items.titleEn: Nvidia CEO encourages Europe's lagging AI sector and offers tools to accelerate data center buildout
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urged players in Europe's lagging artificial intelligence industry to get going and touted a modular system to quickly build AI data centers he says are sorely needed by developers on the continent. In an upbeat speech Wednesday at a company conference for developers and investors in Berlin, Huang also laid out tools to keep AI applications from running amok by confining them in a digital "sandbox."

Gold gains, silver slips as oil prices rise, Fed rate hike expectations persist - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold prices were slightly higher and spot silver prices were lower in early U.S. trading Wednesday, as renewed concerns about energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz and persistent expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening weighed on precious metals. Gold found some support from lower Treasury yields and defensive demand, while silver struggled to sustain Tuesday's recovery amid uncertainty surrounding industrial activity and the interest rate outlook. At the time of the latest verified morning price reading, spot gold was trading near $4,136.70 an ounce, up $12.60, or 0.31%, while spot silver was trading near $57.510, down $0.370, or 0.64%. Market positioning remains divided between signs of weakening economic activity and stubborn inflation pressure. September consumer prices increased 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually, while producer prices surged 1.3% and 6.3%, respectively. Despite those inflation surprises, traders continue to assign approximately an 83% probability that the Federal Reserve will leave interest rates unchanged at its Oct. 27-28 meeting. Expectations for another rate increase remain concentrated in December, with futures indicating roughly a 94% probability that rates will be higher by the Dec. 9 meeting. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was trading near the 5.1% area Wednesday morning, down from recent highs above 5.3%, as weaker housing activity and concerns about financial-market stability supported government bonds. The dollar's broader resilience and the prospect of additional Fed tightening continue to limit gold's upside potential despite some relief from lower yields.
